title: Sushruta
summary: Sushruta is the traditional author of the Sushruta Samhita, a text on medicine and surgery. Sources place him around Kashi, now Varanasi, and date him to about 600 BCE, though estimates conflict and little is known of his life. Tradition links him to the divine physician Dhanvantari. The text lists over 300 surgical procedures and 120 instruments.

uncertainty.note: Sources give c. 600 BCE or 7th-6th centuries BCE; one says as early as 1000 BCE is unlikely. These are estimates for the figure, not documented life dates.

where.modern_name: Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, India (pinned to the area where sources say he practiced; traditionally Kashi)
where.historical_name: Kashi (Varanasi) on the Ganges, northern India

importance.justification: Author, by tradition, of a foundational Ayurvedic text with over 300 surgical procedures.

sources.title: Journal article on Sushruta (PubMed Central PMC5512402)
sources.publisher: PubMed Central, U.S. National Institutes of Health

reviewer_note: Historicity and dates are uncertain; descent from Dhanvantari is tradition and the PMC article treats it as belief. World History Encyclopedia says the link to a Mahabharata Sushruta is not accepted by most scholars. PMC article title not recorded; described by ID. Pin is a city centroid.
